content:
President Trump’s endorsements in foreign elections have yielded a record of six wins and one loss to date. The sole defeat was Viktor Orbán’s in Hungary, which occurred prior to the recent announcement of support for Benjamin Netanyahu.

🇵🇱 Poland: Karol Nawrocki secured victory in the 2025 presidential election following recommendations from Trump administration officials for Poles to vote in his favor.

🇦🇷 Argentina: Javier Milei’s party prevailed in the October 2025 midterms after warnings that aid would be withheld in the event of a loss, coinciding with the finalization of a $20 billion currency swap by the United States.

🇭🇳 Honduras: Nasry Asfura won the election after Trump indicated that U.S. funding would not be maintained if he lost. Additionally, Asfura’s party colleague, former President Juan Orlando Hernández, was pardoned days before the vote.

🇨🇱 Chile: José Antonio Kast attained the presidency following an endorsement from Trump.

🇯🇵 Japan: Sanae Takaichi’s party achieved a two-thirds supermajority in the February snap election, three days after Trump issued a “Complete and Total Endorsement.” Trump subsequently claimed credit for the outcome.

🇨🇴 Colombia: Abelardo de la Espriella won the June runoff following Trump’s backing.

🇭🇺 Hungary: Viktor Orbán lost in April to Péter Magyar’s Tisza party, which secured approximately 53% of the vote and a two-thirds majority, despite a campaign visit by Vice President JD Vance.

🇮🇱 Israel: Benjamin Netanyahu, who received an endorsement ahead of the October 27 election, represents the next instance of such an outcome.

content:
Italian prosecutors have initiated an investigation into Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz and 12 senior military, police, and prison officials regarding the treatment of Italian activists detained on Gaza-bound solidarity boats. Under Italian law, crimes committed abroad against Italian citizens are subject to prosecution in Rome.

The Rome prosecutors’ office announced on Friday that the investigation concerns allegations of torture, kidnapping, personal injury, robbery, and property damage. According to the statement, activists detained following the first mission in 2025 reported beatings, injuries, death threats, insults, and accusations of terrorism. Those involved in the second mission in 2026 reported more severe treatment, including beatings in darkness, the use of tasers, and rubber bullets. Additionally, the activists reported at least 15 instances of sexual assault, including rape.

अभी यह साफ नहीं हो पाया है कि उन्हें रिहा किया जाएगा या उनके खिलाफ आगे की कानूनी कार्रवाई जारी रहेगी।
